pages.title: A phone inside the story
paragraphs: Give players a phone they can open in chat: installed apps, changing shortcuts, an App Store, nested business lists and narrator-generated service pages. A restaurant can lead to its menu, a job board to an offer, and a contact app to a conversation while the surrounding game continues.

Scripts own the installed-app list, shortcuts, selected app, configured directory entries, discovery filters, layout preference and reveal flags. The narrator presents those screens and generates page contents. The host game owns purchases, items, messages, appointments, contracts, quests and their consequences.

This is a single-player narrative interface. It is not a separate web app, a fixed-width phone image, a transaction engine or an authoritative alarm scheduler. The current adapter leaves phone state unchanged when it cannot identify exactly one player.
table: Open the app currently assigned D, from Home
Browse a configured page or contextual detail
pages.note: Suggested first test: phone → phone store → phone open Maps → phone view nearby. Ordinary narration and the host clock continue; browsing can consume story time.

pages.title: Install without replacing your world
paragraphs: 1. Make a test remix and preserve its complete export. In Voyage Studio, open Content and the JSON editor. At the Content root, use Download initial GameState JSON. A save-game state export is a different artifact.

2. Open the included generic-phone-installer.html locally. Choose your complete world JSON, then Prepare updated world. Review the counts and Download updated world JSON. This page has no network requests and does not change the original file or your live world.

3. In the test remix, return to the Content root JSON editor. Replace the complete JSON with the complete prepared export, then Save. Do not paste the small phone-mod.json over your entire world: that file contains only the phone records.

4. Copy or export the saved complete world again. Check that the existing locations, starts, quests, lore and non-phone triggers remain. Create a new game and test the listed phone commands, your custom apps and ordinary gameplay.

The merger replaces the phone_mod_ namespace as one complete profile and prepends the narrator bridge once. It keeps other world fields. A conflicting earlier phone bridge produces a review error instead of silently stacking instructions.
pages.note: The command-line merger is an alternative using Node 20+. It refuses to overwrite an existing output or the original input. Native Mods → Apply has not been verified for this release; direct complete-export merging is the verified installation route. Existing saves are not migrated.

pages.title: Choose the settings that matter
paragraphs: Edit config/generic-phone.json, then rebuild. The starting apps are Messages, Maps, Food Delivery and App Store. Clock is configured but disabled; creators can enable it after connecting a suitable time system. Corner Cafe is an example: replace its catalogue entry with a business from your own world.
table: Default Home layout for a new phone: false=single, true=paired. Existing players keep their stored choice.
Per app: false omits it from the built mod; true or omitted enables it. Includes App Store.
Enabled app IDs installed on a new phone. Include App Store when enabled.
The app that opens the scripted download catalogue.
Per app: public, or triggered until revealed. This is separate from business discovery.
Per app: false protects it from uninstall. App Store is always protected.
Per app: known, all_public, or curated.
Per app: exact location/area exclusions and optional messages.
Optional name of a compact public clock record in host script storage.
paragraphs_after: Use stable IDs when renaming labels. The app label is what players type; the ID owns saved installation state. Reordering the catalogue does not intentionally reassign an existing valid shortcut. A removed configuration ID is pruned from that player’s phone the next time it is processed.
pages.note: Known means the world regards a named entity as known; it does not mean visited. The current native adapter rejects the visited listing mode. Device possession is not required and no invented device-availability flag is used.

pages.title: Turn any app on or off
paragraphs: Every app, including App Store, supports enabled:true or enabled:false. Omitted means true for older configurations. Disabled apps are excluded during the build: their app instructions and business data are not shipped. A story reveal cannot enable an excluded app.

Use enabled:false to turn an app off. Use enabled:true with triggered visibility for an app that should exist but remain hidden until an event. Starting installation and player uninstall protection remain independent.
Disabling App Store removes its Home control and disables install/remove commands. Other preinstalled enabled apps still work. The Store must be in initialInstalledIds when enabled.

Rebuild both generated files, merge into a test world and start a fresh save. Existing world saves are not automatically updated. After an explicit script update, removed IDs are pruned at the next phone request; re-enabling does not reinstall them in that existing registry.
table: enabled:true; visibility public; omit initial ID
enabled:true; visibility triggered; omit initial ID
Starts off. Enable after connecting a suitable host time system.
pages.note: The switch controls this module. Independent world lore and narration may still mention the service. Do not treat it as a guaranteed narrative ban. The six new enablement tests run the generated scripts offline; the new master switch has not yet been exercised live.

pages.title: Add a custom app
paragraphs: Add an object to the apps array with a unique id, label and order. This example adds a transit app that can be downloaded. To preinstall it in a new game, also add transit to initialInstalledIds.
paragraphs_after: Generated pages use phone view routes. An activity page uses phone choose request ticket. Opening the app itself does not select the activity.

The short summary appears in the Store and opening menu. Give it a concrete purpose: a name alone can lead the narrator to invent the wrong kind of service. Put general service rules in app.guidance and page-specific work in page.guidance. Keep the host’s existing rules in force.
pages.note: Use examples/transit-app.json for copying. To continue inside a generated menu, the player can use ordinary language. A generated phone view detail also retains the current app context, but it is model-mediated browsing rather than a new deterministic transaction command.

pages.title: Business lists and generated menus
paragraphs: A directory is a curated set of candidate businesses attached to one app. All public means all entries marked public in that configured set; it does not scan every store in the world. The same world location can participate in several apps with different policies.
table: Public entries whose exact locationId passes known-entity
Every public entry in this app’s configured catalogue
Public entries also listed in directory.curatedIds
paragraphs_after: For a curated list, add "curatedIds": ["corner-cafe"]. Set public:false to exclude a candidate from every listing mode. Add a page with kind:directory and optionally use openPage to open it immediately.

The listed number selects that business. The narrator then generates offerings and indicative prices. Numbers inside that generated menu are interpreted by narration and do not select another business. Back returns from menu to list, then from list to Home.
pages.note: Descriptions are catalogue data. Explain what the business sells; do not hide engine instructions in them. Generated offerings and prices are not cached by this module. Use examples/store-app.json.

pages.title: Delivery rules belong to each app
paragraphs: Configure exclusions independently for each app. An area-specific message takes precedence over a whole-location rule; otherwise the app message is used. Location and area IDs must match the host’s native values exactly.
paragraphs_after: phone delivery check tests the player’s current location and area in the currently open delivery app. It reports an exclusion, a missing destination, or that the destination is not excluded. The check does not place a new order.

Not excluded is narrower than available: opening hours, stock, service coverage, funds, weather, fees and arrival estimates still belong to the host service. Natural-language ordering receives the app’s exclusions as context. An alternative destination must be checked under those same rules.

This module can deterministically select and emit the refusal message. It cannot guarantee that every host model will obey it or veto every native purchase writer. Treat it as an integration policy, not an atomic financial guard.
pages.note: There is no shared global blacklist. Giving Food Delivery a blocked location does not block a shopping app. Use examples/store-app.json for a complete editable app; configure both apps separately if both should be restricted.

pages.title: Hidden apps and real unlock triggers
paragraphs: For an enabled app, set appStoreVisibility:triggered and leave it out of initialInstalledIds. The scripted catalogue omits it and the registry rejects a premature installation request. Live narration can still invent a successful installation: this is visibility/state control, not a guaranteed prose restriction. A reveal makes it available; it does not install it or grant account access.
paragraphs_after: Place that script in a creator-authored trigger with the actual quest, event or other supported condition that should reveal the app. The ID signal_vault must equal your app ID. Use the existing player key exactly; it includes JSON string quoting.

Alternatively, set unlockKnownEntity to an exact host entity name. A true known-entity result reveals the app when its phone is next processed. Reveal is persistent in this release; turning a grant back to false does not revoke a reveal that was already recorded.

Public download visibility, installed state and service authorization are separate. A public job app can still require membership before accepting work. Use app/page guidance to connect that service to the world’s existing access rules.
pages.note: examples/hidden-app.json and examples/reveal-trigger.json provide complete records. Replace the example quest condition with your world’s real trigger. The adapter currently requires exactly one player; this example is not multiplayer attribution.

pages.title: Connect the host systems
table: Exactly one action string and one key from check(player-level); state is keyed by JSON.stringify(player name).
check(party-location) and check(party-area); used by Maps and delivery checks.
check(known-entity) for each configured exact locationId. No native historical-visit reader.
Disabled by default. Scripts cannot read the built-in clock. Optional clockStorageKey reads a creator-provided custom storage record for Time page context.
Host-generated transaction and state systems; the phone does not charge, pay or maintain a second ledger.
Host story/state systems; existing relationships, access rules and explicit choices remain relevant.
May supply time and continuity through the host. The generic phone has no required LC dependency.
paragraphs_after: To enable Clock, find app id clock in your profile config and set enabled:true. Its supplied public visibility then allows downloading. Add clock to initialInstalledIds only if it should start installed in new games. Rebuild the mod and installer. LC installation alone does not configure the connection.

For an optional clock adapter, write a small public record such as storage.public_clock = {date:"2040-05-03", time:"09:20"}, then set clockStorageKey:"public_clock". Keep that record short: at most 1000 serialized characters are included. The host adapter must update it before the relevant phone turn; this module does not infer a civil date from game-tick.

Clock Alarms is a generated view, not a new scheduler. If your world requires dependable alarms, connect an existing authoritative event system and verify both the stored event and its later firing. An attractive generated alarm list is insufficient evidence.
pages.note: There is no inventory-based device gate. Renaming a player can create a different phone key. Native multiplayer attribution is unsupported; offline per-name state isolation is not multiplayer support.

pages.title: Build, edit and understand the runtime
pages.code:
node native/build-mod.mjs config/generic-phone.json build/custom-mod.json
node native/merge-world.mjs original.json build/custom-mod.json new-world.json
node --test test/*.test.mjs
table: Validate configuration and build inert data records plus six native handlers. Returns {triggers}.
Return a separate complete world and preservation report; reject saves and conflicting bridges.
Read configuration, attribute the player, restore/prune phone state, allocate stable shortcuts and build screen context.
Home, layout, close/back, install, uninstall and hidden download visibility.
Configured pages, activity choice, directory selection and generated-menu context.
Per-app policy checks and context for natural or generated detail requests.
paragraphs_after: The builder emits phone_mod_config_* and phone_mod_data_* records as JSON inside inert script comments, read with JSON.parse. Runtime triggers use action-text conditions, planning phase and party scope. They use the documented storage, triggers, check, effects and log surfaces; they do not evaluate generated code.

Only edit readable source/configuration, then rebuild. Deployment scripts remove indentation/comments to fit native limits; complete world exports stay pretty-printed. In Studio the generated records are under Content → Mechanics → Advanced → Triggers.
pages.note: No npm dependencies are required. Node 20+ is for rebuilding and the CLI merger, not the Voyage runtime. The supplied HTML installer needs no Node installation, but its browser UI could not be live-tested in the authoring environment.

pages.title: API and persistence reference
table: Case-insensitive exact app label; updates installation revision. Existing host orders/accounts are not deleted by script.
Browse a configured page. An unregistered detail continues inside the current app as model-mediated browsing.
Invoke a configured startsActivity:true page; ordinary page viewing does not invoke it.
Open the current app’s eligible business list / select an exact listed label. phone restaurant NAME is an alias.
Scripted directory menu→list→Home; from other app pages returns Home. Generated labels may claim a different destination.
Installed/revealed IDs, shortcuts, layout, app/page/directory, revision and lastHandled receipt.
Creator grant:true reveals the download on the next processed phone action.
paragraphs_after: The receipt combines game tick and action text to prevent duplicate scripted navigation effects across handlers. A generated detail adds context without inventing a deterministic transaction. Natural conversation does not silently navigate the phone.

Configuration bounds: 32 apps, 12 pages per app, 128 businesses per app, unique lowercase ASCII app IDs up to 48 characters, unique short app labels up to 32 characters, and one-line summaries up to 160 characters. Page names use letters, spaces and hyphens, up to 40 characters. App/page guidance is bounded to 1800 characters each. Commands are limited to 400 characters. The builder also rejects any serialized trigger above 10000 characters.

Changing the starting app list or default layout affects new phone state. Existing state retains its installed IDs and chosen layout, apart from IDs removed from the current catalogue. Start a fresh game when changing profiles; legacy save migration is not provided.
pages.note: Do not install two phone profiles together under the same namespace. Use the complete-profile merger to remove obsolete phone records. Keep unrelated trigger names outside phone_mod_.

pages.title: Test the integration, not just the text
paragraphs: For every important change, compare four layers: the persisted phone state, the emitted instruction, the visible reply and the host’s resulting state. A correct registry does not prove the narrator showed the requested screen; a narrated purchase does not prove the inventory or currency is correct.

Use fresh saves for different starting defaults. Exercise both sides of each setting: paired/single, visible/hidden, before/after reveal, removable/protected, known/public/curated, blocked/allowed and area/default messages. Test a real player request after opening a page, and check that browsing did not accept, buy, hire or travel.
Retain failed trials. A later correct reply does not erase an omitted screen or invented record. Recheck when the model, world guidance, source version or Voyage renderer changes.
table: Narrator omits or changes a screen
Try an exact app command and inspect state. Home can repeat a prior invented app, so returning Home is not a guaranteed recovery.
Use ordinary-language follow-up. phone view details has contextual routing; other invented commands are not guaranteed.
Use clear word-bearing rows and explicitly confirm the quoted total. Inspect native consequences.
Connect authoritative host records if required; generated prose alone is not a stored fact.
Do not advertise support with this adapter.
Use the verified complete-export merge route until Mods → Apply is separately checked.
pages.note: The final release verification sheet lists the actual test results and remaining limitations. No deterministic transaction veto, alarm scheduling guarantee, fixed-width handset frame or universal model compliance is claimed.

pages.title: Optional improvements and sources
paragraphs: Creators can extend the phone without adding a new engine for every app. Start with a short purpose and one useful page, then add only the host connections the experience requires.
bullets: Author a merchant catalogue per service, including location IDs, useful descriptions and discovery policy.
Add a transit, journal, club, guild, weather, medical appointment or property app using generated pages and existing host systems.
Reveal an app through a quest, invitation or known place; keep download visibility separate from account permission.
Add an authoritative menu/cart/order or alarm adapter if exact persistence matters. This is extra implementation, not an undocumented built-in feature.
Provide explicit profile candidates or service eligibility data where broad narrator guidance is too variable.
Choose the starting apps and delivery messages that suit each world. A smaller catalogue usually makes the first phone interaction easier to read.
pages.note: Source basis: previously acquired Latitude documentation and production Studio/runtime observations, September 2026, engine 36. Prompt/context guidance was consulted before changing consumers. The module is independently authored integration code, not an official Latitude feature or guarantee. MIT covers the original TextPhone code and documentation. Third-party world material and assets remain separate and are not relicensed by this project.

pages.title: Verification: controls and configuration
pages.lead: 0.5.0 | Bounded production trials and offline tests
paragraphs: Tested on production Voyage engine 36 with a Living Continuity host; Story DeepSeek 3.2, Character Moderate, State Ultra. Results concern this integration and configuration. They are not a guarantee for another model or world.
table: Saved setting and exact emitted rows pass. Paired rows rendered correctly; later single-column requests sometimes still rendered paired. Visible behavior is inconsistent.
Live install, remove and reinstall changed the registry. A new app whose preferred key was occupied received a different key; typing that key opened it.
Core Store refusal displayed correctly. Custom removable:false retained the app, but narration falsely claimed uninstall, including after a placement retry.
Controlled native lists exercised all three policies. Unknown businesses were filtered only in the known app; a separate public list and curated subset remained independent.
Live blocked/unblocked apps and distinct refusal messages passed. Area-specific wording took precedence. Whole-location fallback and missing-address branches also passed offline.
Live premature install refused; trigger grant made the download available; explicit install then succeeded. Immediate reveal narration was wrong. Known-entity reveal also passed offline.
Live shortcut and phone choose routed the intended page. It waited for a choice, but invented an invalid contact and controls. Routing passes; generated choice quality is limited.
A fresh tab reopened the same saved game; layout, installed apps, reveals and shortcuts matched exactly.
Native time/location pages were exercised. Optional clockStorageKey passed offline; no direct structured LC clock adapter is configured in the supplied profile.
pages.note: Player layout commands are distinct from creator configuration options. Directory policy, protection, delivery and visibility are edited in configuration and rebuilt. Testing retains failed replies rather than counting correct script state as a complete visual pass.

pages.title: Verification: scope and remaining limits
paragraphs: All nine world-profile apps and their configured pages were exercised. Trials covered messaging/jobs/calls, time/alarms, maps/directions, food menus/orders, shopping browse/cart/orders/stores, social profiles/messages, responder listings/hiring inquiries and restricted marketplace account/listings. Browsing and explicit follow-up were checked separately.

Two quote-to-confirmation purchase trials produced the expected native currency deductions only after explicit confirmation. No automatic job acceptance or responder hire was established in those browse/inquiry trials. Delivery arrival, long-term order memory, alarm firing, relationship outcomes and the complete employment lifecycle are host gameplay, not proven by these tests.

Observed model failures include omitted screens, retained paired rows after a single-column request, false removal notices, lost field labels, invented alarm defaults, unauthored account routes, invented controls and a wrong app inventory description that survived reinstall. A requested tracking quest was not created. No atomic transaction guard or authoritative generated ledger is provided.

The final source passes 72 offline checks: 23 current native-script checks, three complete-export merge checks, two synthetic installer-event checks and 44 retained prototype/component checks. The distributed generic package contains 11 relevant checks; the world package contains 28. The older 44 checks are historical evidence, not proof of the current native display.

The complete-export merge route was applied to the private test world and its complete saved JSON matched the generated result after reload. Existing host content was preserved. The same merge code and generic profile were tested offline. Native Mods → Apply and public mod publication were not validated.

The local HTML installer's merge logic and event flow passed synthetic checks. Browser policy blocked opening its local file in the authoring environment, so its live browser interface was not verified. The command-line route uses the same tested merger. A requested narrow viewport did not change the observed browser dimensions; mobile wrapping remains unverified.

Multiplayer attribution is unsupported. The adapter leaves phone state unchanged when there is not exactly one attributable player; independent-name offline checks do not establish multiplayer support. Older phone saves are not automatically migrated. Revalidate after changing the host instructions, model, routing, catalogue or platform renderer.
pages.note: Use this as a configurable narrative interface with known presentation limits. Exact visible output and durable service records require further platform/host integration; those guarantees are not implied by the package.

pages.title: Vanilla compatibility and hidden Clock
paragraphs: September 30, 2026: the distributed complete-export merger was applied to a fresh vanilla remix of source revision 176. The native saved full world matched the prepared output. All 63 host triggers, 227 locations and 19 starts were preserved; 23 phone records and the exact narrator prefix were added.

The new single-player vanilla save used Sonnet 4.5 Story with High character and state settings. This trial used the predecessor hidden-download configuration. The new master enabled switch is tested offline only; no native deployment or visual guarantee for it is claimed.

Initial Home displayed the four configured apps without Clock. An explicit phone install Clock request was refused in the saved registry and emitted Story instruction, but narration falsely claimed installation. The next Home repeated the invented Clock icon. Hiding an app controls the registry, not every sentence the model may generate.

The release has 36 world-package checks and 17 generic-package checks, including every app independently off, all apps off, App Store off, stale active selection, invalid flags and reveal resistance. Source configurations remain editable; generated artifacts include only enabled apps.
table: Pass: exact host preservation and saved-output equality.
Pass: absent from initial installed IDs and unrevealed download catalogue.
Fail: narration claimed success despite refusal; Home carried it forward.
Offline verified for both profiles. Live time accuracy/adapter not tested.

Meal directory and numbered menu selection worked; a permitted shopping-app installation opened its correct service menu. Final native state retained the installation, unchanged currency and one phone inventory item. Other service consequences were not retested here.
pages.note: Native Mods > Apply, automatic save migration and multiplayer remain unverified or unsupported as stated. No new alarm scheduler or access to Voyage's native clock is provided.

pages.title: Creator installation checklist
paragraphs: Check these steps on your own test remix. Checkmarks record your review, not a guarantee of model behavior.
checklist: Preserve a complete original world export and make a test remix.
Choose one profile and replace synthetic catalogue entries where needed.
Use exact native location/area IDs and distinct app names and IDs.
Set starting apps, discovery policy and each app’s delivery messages.
Rebuild both the mod JSON and HTML installer after configuration changes.
Merge the complete export, save it in the test remix and read it back.
Confirm original lore, NPCs, locations, quests and host triggers remain.
Start a fresh save; open every app/page and test each chosen toggle.
Test reveal before/after, install/remove, shortcuts and save/reload.
Check narration AND saved state for consequential actions.
Read the verification limits before sharing or using the profile.
